1031249.ReadingBookDes:
My children, if you can hear the call of the ancestral spirit, then you have been blessed beyond measure.
Now that you have stepped onto the path of the priesthood, understand this: To be named an assistant priest is both an honor-and a responsibility.

You must now open your eyes like newborn beasts, and cleanse your ears like the first meltwater of spring.

At dawn, you will follow the priest who guides you, helping prepare the rituals of each season. You will listen to ancient prayers and memorize every detail of every rite. At dusk, you will labor: storing grain, tanning hides, assisting hunts... Set aside your restlessness, your pride. Every moment of your days is a lesson.
This is not punishment. It is the ancestral spirit refining your heart, and the first step toward learning the ancient wisdom of Kanamia.

The knowledge of a priest is not found in scrolls. It lives in the words of your mentors, in the details of each ceremony, and in the daily rhythm of the tribe. Those with quick minds may grasp it early. Those slower to understand, if their hearts are sincere, will also be guided by the ancestral spirit in time.

If you are wise enough, and strong enough, your priest will see it in you. The High Priestess will come to know your name. And then, and only then, will you be worthy to take up the true mantle of priesthood, and become a bridge between our people and the ancestral spirit.

The path is not easy. But since the ancestral spirit has chosen you, you shall not turn away from the calling. Go now. See with your own eyes. Listen with your own ears. And feel with your heart.

Warning from an Elder

1031250.ReadingBookDes:
They are wanderers without a manifesto. The more prosperous Asterleeds becomes, the lighter their packs grow.

As the brick walls of this trade city climb ever higher, As the scent of fish is washed from the port by the weight of coin, As the stone steps of Ocean Hill gleam from a thousand soles... They choose to leave. They sell what they own, give up their jobs, tuck an old coat into a cloth bundle, or simply walk away with nothing at all.

Purposes? Must it always be so utilitarian? Wiping down every window in the city, Scraping barnacles off the hulls of every fishing boat, Measuring the Regnus Coast with the soles of their feet... Do these count as "purposes"?

1031251.BookName: A Letter to the Chief Priest
1031251.ReadingBookDes:
To the Esteemed Chief Priest,

Greetings. Today, while visiting the Council Library, I came across a book titled "The Founding of Asterleeds," and nearly dropped my holy emblem in shock. Nowhere in the entire volume is the Divine's blessing of our land mentioned. The First Oracle's Revelation is completely ignored, as though it never happened!

The book attributes every achievement to the artisans, even claiming the ancient Legacies were built by them alone. This is a desecration. Even the toddlers along Asterleeds' cobbled roads know: those Legacies were granted to the artisans by the Creed, under the Divine's will. And yet, the author erases the Divine and the Creed as if we were never part of our city's founding.

Worse still, this heretical nonsense is shelved openly in the main hall of the Council.

I humbly ask you to assign someone to investigate the authorship of this text. And, if possible, to request the Council prohibit its circulation. I have marked the most offensive passages in red and enclosed them with this letter.

Additionally, I've already instructed my subordinates to begin looking into the author. I await your guidance on how to proceed.

In service to the Creed, Evans, Priest of the Asterleeds Diocese

1031252.ReadingBookDes:
Oh please. Those scavengers who go on and on about "freedom" and "no rules"? Give me a break. Out on the Asteria Plains, where the fangs and claws are real, trust me, they know rules better than anyone.

Then you've got those ones at the resting post. Pretty harmless, really. By day, they hawk trinkets dug out of ruins at their rickety stalls by Andra Resting Post. By night, they either cram into the drafty huts or just roll up in blankets and sleep out under the stars. They're less scavengers and more... really bad peddlers.

And then there's the worst bunch, the Drifters. They cluster in twos or threes, tossing around grand talk like "mapping the land of Regnus with our feet," noses pointed sky-high. But you peek in their pouches and hey-just enough coin to be smug. Word is, one of them has ties to the Merchant Guild... I'd bet on it. 1031254.ReadingBookDes:
You ask me who I prefer doing business with? Not the Merchant Guild. Those folks have more tricks than a bird has feathers. Street vendors? Forget it. They'll haggle over every last coin. The Fishers' Guild is alright. Honest folk. But I don't deal in seafood, so not much overlap there.

No, I prefer the scavengers. They're out on the plains every day with a heavy pack on their back, always bumping into rocks, thorns, and bad luck, so they've got to stock up on my medical supplies. They always need firestarters, and more often than not, they top off their lamp oil or grab a coil of sturdy rope before heading out again.
And the best part? They don't haggle. Ever. They hand over a list, drop the coin, grab their gear, and walk. Now that-that's what I call refreshing.

What? You're asking where they get their money? Okay, fine... I've done a little digging.
Don't give me that look.
I worry too, alright? Last thing I want is the Defense Corps knocking on my door while I'm serving tainted coin.

Turns out, some of these scavengers are master leatherworkers. That fine leather coat worn by a city noble? Might've been stitched together by one of these folks. Others make their coin collecting junk on the road-stuff most people toss out-and either sell it to passing merchants or peddle it here in the city. And you know what? After they clean it up and patch it together, it actually looks... kinda nice. Tempting, even.
And if all else fails... Well, rumor has it some scavengers come from money. Playing scavenger is just their version of "living free." Not my place to judge.

Now, sure, there are a few who swipe things now and then. Lazy types who want a shortcut. But around here, us merchants have a system. One glance, a raised eyebrow, and we know who to keep an eye on.

1031255.BookName: To all visitors to the ruins of Andra Landing Battle
1031255.ReadingBookDes:
Scavengers, take heed:
Yes, there are wartime Legacies scattered along this beach-modules, armor, even unopened supply crates. But beside every "treasure," you may find an unexploded shell, a malfunctioning relic, or a cloud of poison gas.
Marco. Eri. Jokebo. They once walked this shore, confident as you are. Now, all that remains of them... are their names.

Before you step forward, ask yourself:
Can you tell a dud shell from a supply cache?
Can you recognize the sickly-sweet stench of toxic mist?
Can you guarantee that come sunrise, your friends won't be reading your name to an empty sky?

Mourners, this is not your altar:
True remembrance belongs in the Statue of the Hero. If your grief burns unquenched...
Write to the Council!
(Scrawl with the angriest pen, the clumsiest letters, and ask them when they plan to clean up this battlefield rot.)

Tourists, eyes up:
The giant golem arm is the safest place for a scenic view.
You'll see the whole battlefield-and still have all your limbs to go home with.
Still tempted to touch the sands below? Think of the ones who vanished, whose bodies grew suddenly half as light.

Cove, Survivor of Asterleeds Independence War

1031256.ReadingBookDes:
At first, no one paid much attention to the delicate white flowers blooming in silence.
It wasn't until scavengers on the Asteria Plains took note that anyone realized something strange was happening: the once-barren edge of the old battlefield had begun to blossom-tiny white petals scattered like stars. Botanists were called in to examine the phenomenon. What they discovered left everyone speechless: These were peaceflowers, a rare medicinal herb native only to the Duchy of Byrnhald, usually found growing at the foot of snow-covered mountains.
More disturbing still-the area where the flowers flourished most densely was precisely the site of the Andra Landing Battle. It was here, years ago, that fallen Byrnhald soldiers were buried in the field without ceremony.
Cautiously, the scholars brushed aside the flowering stems. Beneath the damp, black soil, they uncovered uniform buttons that were still intact, not yet fully decayed. The roots of the flowers had taken hold deep in the old shell craters.
"So that's it..." An elderly scholar removed his glasses with trembling hands. "These enemy soldiers... they've bloomed peace in another form." "

1031257.BookName: The Mine Tunnel That Appears at Night
1031257.ReadingBookDes:
Kingsley: Shh... Have you heard? That mine tunnel that only appears at "night"...
Will: Nonsense! This dump only has two states—where the searchlights shine and where they don't!
Kingsley: What if... "night" is when the lights go out?
Will: Don't you dare—
Kingsley: Hey wait, why are the lights flickering? Did you forget to refi—Ah!!!
Will: Kingsley? You, [Byrnhald Vulgarity], stop messing around!
...
Kingsley?
Kingsley!!!

1031258.BookName: The Art of Absolute Tongue I
1031258.ReadingBookDes:
We must strengthen our cooperation and work together as one.
Because the core of teamwork is cooperation—only by working together can we bring out the true value of the team.

1031259.ReadingBookDes:
When people think of the Bahamar Highlands, the first impression is always solemn, austere, and imposing. This comes not only from the drastic elevation changes and harsh highland climate, but also from the Pillar of Divinity hanging high in the sky—like a vigilant gaze watching over this land. Together, these elements form the grand background of the highlands.

Today, we'll be discussing the marvel born from this majestic landscape: the Needle Rocks. Every traveler who has set foot on the Bahamar Highlands must have been impressed by them. Their shapes are strange and abrupt—nothing like natural formations, more like the barbs on some vicious beast. Most striking of all is how uniform they are in appearance, as if some historic event transformed the highlands into fertile ground for their growth.

Yet the origins of these rocks remain widely debated, with no definitive conclusion even today. Captivated by the Needle Rocks, the author spent several years on the Bahamar Highlands collecting theories about their formation. Below are some of the leading explanations:

1031260.ReadingBookDes:
Wanted: Hammersmith Geronimo
Crime: Unauthorized use of Bapharian Legacy
Bounty: 100,000 Luno

Description:
· Usually dressed like a craftsman; wears a monocle.
· Carries a modified craftsman's hammer on his back.
· Wears a customized exoskeleton mech.

Summary of Crimes:
This suspect is a senior member of the illegal highland organization "Cabbage Mission." He secretly excavated and modified Bapharian Legacy​ in an attempt to bypass the Creed's supervision. Under the guise of "testing modified legacy," he deployed altered Golems across the highlands, causing rampages and injuries. He also helped his associates install modified components onto weapons, resulting in severe injuries among several craftsmen and Defense Corps soldiers.

Warning:
This hammersmith always carries Bapharian Legacy​ with him. The small ocular legacy he modified may appear harmless, but it is extremely dangerous. If spotted, maintain distance—do not approach or attempt to apprehend him. Report his whereabouts to the Creed or the Defense Corps immediately.

1031261.BookName: Volume I: The Highland Calamity and the Ancient Seal
1031261.ReadingBookDes:
Legend has it that two hundred years ago, followers of the witch Hruga appeared on the Bahamar Highlands and unleashed a terrifying ​Void Engram, seeking to annihilate humanity... At that time, humans were no match for Hruga. After one crushing defeat after another, human civilization stood on the brink of annihilation.
In a moment of desperation, the Creed guided emissaries of the Bapharian Divines to the highlands. With the help of the deities, Hruga was finally defeated and sealed.

However, her power scattered across the Bahamar Highlands, severely disrupting the flow of Engram​ here.
The most immediate manifestation is the growth of Illusory Bloom—a sinister crystalline with an otherworldly appearance, still widespread across the highlands. Its crystalline shell is nearly impervious, with remarkable regenerative ability, making it almost impossible to destroy completely. Illusory Bloom thus stands as a lasting mark of that ancient war, continuing to threaten the lives of the local inhabitants.

1031262.ReadingBookDes:

A village balancing secular life and faith, founded by Pilgrims from across the continent.
This village is more than just a place to rest—it is a meeting point of intelligence and experience.
Travelers from all lands can share a single loaf of bread without friction, whether they are from Byrnhald, Asterleeds, or the Evergreen Desert.

/-Ascetics' Retreat-/
An ideal place to cultivate one's will!
Though the highland soil is poor and crops struggle to grow, some Ascetics believe that farming strengthens the heart of faith.
Day after day, they try to grow different crops, finally making citrus bloom from stone fissures!
Work alongside them in the fields, or savor the fruits of their labor—they will not hold back.

1031263.ReadingBookDes:
I. Theory of Xeno Engram​ Contamination

It is said that the highlands were once the place where the witch Hruga fell. After her defeat, the Engram​ she released scattered across the land, severely disrupting the local ecosystem. Illusory Bloom, Crimson Marrow Core... Many originally harmless natural materials mutated under the influence of this Engram​. The Needle Rocks may well be one such mutation.

If you think about it, these rocks really do seem to have sprouted in unnervingly uniform patterns, almost like an extreme form of biological rejection. Their sharp spines look as though they're sounding a warning of some kind.

And this theory is not entirely unfounded. Although the highlands border the Asteria Plains, many minerals on the plains have indeed undergone mutation. These mutations go far beyond altered appearances—they involve complete structural reorganization: dense internal matter becoming porous and loose; once-smooth surfaces turning rough and filled with cavities... All these precedents suggest that Needle Rocks, too, may have been affected. Thus, the theory that ordinary ridge stones were "honed" into Needle Rocks feels perfectly plausible.

If you're fascinated by military culture, this is the place for you! The entire station is strictly guarded by the garrison, and the atmosphere is so solemn it could silence both a quarreling Goblin and a Muku.
Meanwhile, the nearby commercial street provides all necessary supplies—don't forget to pick up some "slag" souvenirs.

Perhaps the best spot to feel the presence of the Pillar of Divinity! Perfect for sketching!

When the wind sweeps through the ancient ruins and blends with Priest Lothar's resonant voice, you may find yourself hearing the echo of your own spirit.

At that moment, you must cover your ears, or you'll lose your senses...
Chasing the song, you walk and walk... walk and walk... walk and walk...

1031266.BookName: New Approaches to Post-Plague Intervention I
1031266.ReadingBookDes:
I. Background & Issues


Recently, cases of Illusory Plague calamities have surged on the Bahamar Highlands, all traced back to an evil crystalline entity known as Illusory Bloom. Researchers from all fields have rushed to the highlands to study it, hoping to resolve the calamities at their source. However, while many scholars focus solely on how to destroy the Illusory Bloom, they have overlooked the survivors of the Illusory Plague.

Though these survivors escaped with their lives, the aftereffects have been devastating: some are tormented by nightmares and cannot sleep for days; some lose all joy, haunted constantly by terrifying visions; still others withdraw completely, unable to step outside the safety of their homes ever again.

Therefore, I intend to explore a completely different approach—one that shifts attention toward the survivors themselves. Instead of focusing only on the Illusory Bloom, we must find ways to heal the wounds left on the survivors' hearts.

Note: This is only an experiment—a guiding approach intended to provide a possible direction forward.

1031267.BookName: Volume II: The Witch's Hatred Unveiled
1031267.ReadingBookDes:
Why does Witch Hruga harbor such deep hatred for humanity, vowing their extinction? The answer lies with an almost-forgotten evil race: the Igdias.
This ancient race, existing since the ancient age like the Bapharian Divines, was both arrogant and malevolent. They proclaimed themselves the sole rulers of the Continent of Magna and opposed the Bapharian Divines.
According to the Creed's records, the Igdias once waged a massive war against the Bapharian Divines and attempted to manipulate humans into opposing the deities, but their schemes were ultimately exposed.
After their defeat, internal power struggles erupted within the Igdias, ultimately leading to their downfall...
Tragically, the surviving Igdias placed the blame on humans. The remnants obsessively believed that human betrayal caused their defeat, triggering internal chaos, and thus held humans responsible for the annihilation of their race.
Witch Hruga became the leader of this hardline faction.

1031268.ReadingBookDes:
Dear Mr. Wilp,
I hope this letter reaches you without disturbing your refined pleasure in observing the clouds above Lallipar—after all, judging by the passion in your previous letter, which was filled with elaborate prose yet mentioned scarcely a single practical matter, cloud-watching must indeed be an important and mentally taxing "task."

Moreover, your unique insights regarding the strange scratches on the village's old tree and their connection to the neighboring hawk have left us in awe. A passage describing the color of the neighbor's newly hatched chicks is so vivid that I nearly wanted to clip the description of "that speckled hen's distinctive gait" to keep as... well, a model of a unique literary style.

However, allow me, as a friend, to offer a candid reminder: the Asterleeds has recently been plagued by ​Void Engram​s, and the Pioneer Bureau has been stretched thin dealing with monsters and Engram anomalies. Our ink and time must be devoted to recording the very threats and disasters.

If there are no such pressing matters, please do continue enjoying the tranquility of Lallipar, and consider using your keen observation and vivid writing where they are most needed.

Thank you for your attention to the Pioneer Bureau, and may you discover new curiosities each day.

Note: Without an official assignment or appointment, please refrain from visiting the Pioneer Bureau, to avoid a futile trip.

Pioneer Bureau - Reception
Valeria

1031274.ReadingBookDes:
II. The Theory of the Pillar of Divinity's Influence

However, some Pilgrims hold a different view. They argue that Witch Hruga has been sealed for centuries, her power long since faded, and that—with the Creed's guidance—the land is gradually recovering. The Illusory Bloom has been contained, and the mining of Crimson Marrow was banned long ago... After hundreds of years, the sharp edges of the Needle Rocks should have been worn smooth by the highlands' bitter cold winds.
Yet these rocks remain pristine. Scholars who have studied their internal structure found clear growth layers within, indicating that the Needle Rocks are continuing to grow, at an extremely slow rate. This suggests that their formation is not being sustained by the witch's lingering power, but by a stable and continuous energy source.
It is an energy that predates the witch, so the most evident source is the highlands' defining landmark—the Pillar of Divinity.
The Pillar of Divinity is the largest, most magnificent, and best-preserved creation of the Bapharian Divines on the Continent of Magna. Even after the deities departed, it remains suspended in midair, steadfast against the howling winds. Scholars believe that the pillar continues to supply energy in some form—and that this energy is the true force behind the formation of the Needle Rocks.
Decisive support for this hypothesis comes from Pilgrims' accounts: most Needle Rocks appear to grow in the direction of the Pillar of Divinity.

1031275.ReadingBookDes:
The Illusory Bloom is a dangerous flower found throughout the entire highlands—its colors vibrant, yet hiding a deadly threat.
Those who draw near it are affected by its unique Engram​, which instantly disrupts the flow of their Bio-Engram. Their inner anxieties and fears are then amplified, trapping them in the most terrifying illusions—unable to break free.
This has nothing to do with courage, because the terror comes from your own imagination. Whatever you fear—fear so deeply it cuts to the bone—the more that fear grips you. In short... there is no escape.

This overwhelming terror deals near-fatal damage to the body. For those physically frail, death may come on the spot. Yet the most frightening aspect is that anyone ensnared by the illusion completely loses control of their own body. Only a clear-headed companion can drag you away from the bloom's vicinity; otherwise, the illusions will continue to assault you until your mind and strength are entirely exhausted.

Even for those who manage to escape, the damage to their psyche is often permanent. In the years that follow, those nightmares will cling to them like a restless shadow—surging forth at the height of their happiness, or murmuring ceaselessly in the silence of midnight...

1031276.BookName: New Approaches to Post-Plague Intervention II
1031276.ReadingBookDes:
II. The Similarities Between Illusions and Dreams


First of all, we all know that the Illusory Bloom induces absolute illusions—visions woven entirely by the victim themselves. Those ensnared by their effects often cannot escape, sinking deeper into nightmares of their own making.

Yet frightening as they are, illusions are ultimately born from the projections of one's own mind. In this sense, they are strikingly similar to another intangible phenomenon that also exerts influence over the mind: dreams.
To ordinary people, dreams are private and immutable. Some may bring up lucid dreaming—indeed, it is a common form of intervention, but its effectiveness is limited and its success rate, low. What I am referring to, however, is something far more concrete: the ability to enter another person's dream, and to intervene within it as naturally as one would in daily life.

This is not fantasy; it is something I have witnessed with my own eyes. In Asterleeds—despite its pride in technological advancement—such a feat has not yet been achieved. But a tribe that neither relies on ancient legacy nor worships gears has done exactly that—the Kanamia Tribe. Through techniques passed down through generations, they can not only influence others' dreams, but connect multiple dreamers together, forming a shared, tangible dreamspace.

Yes, this is not lucid dreaming, but co-dreaming. Or rather, experiencing the dream as vividly as reality itself.

1031278.ReadingBookDes:
III. The Discovery of Unknown Scars

However, the second hypothesis also contains aspects that are difficult to explain. The Needle Rocks' sharp, abrupt forms do not resemble an act of reverence or devotion; rather, they appear more like a warning. Scholars claim that the Needle Rocks grow in the direction of the Pillar of Divinity—could this be suggesting that the Divine clan's legacy caused nature itself to evolve into such jagged, alien structures?

More critically, these Needle Rocks are not, as scholars assert, growing toward the Pillar of Divinity like some phototropic plants. Based on my own investigations, only a small number of Needle Rocks point toward the Pillar of Divinity, while the majority exhibit distribution and orientation patterns that resemble random evolution.

In addition, I have discovered numerous abandoned Bapharian Ruins that had suffered catastrophic destruction. The wounds carved into these ruins remain shocking even to this day. This seems to hint at a brutal, long-buried history of the Bahamar Highlands. Since the formation of the Needle Rocks is thought to be connected to external stimuli, then these hidden events must also be taken into consideration.

1031279.ReadingBookDes:
My name is Ismark, an ordinary craftsman of Asterleeds.
Every day, I repeat the same routine:
Preheat the legacy,
Adjust the parameters and pull the starter...
Wait for the result...

Repeating this cycle day after day has drained me completely. It feels as though I can already see the end of my life from here!

Until I joined the "Pilgrimage to Bahamar." Everything changed...
At the Ascetics' Retreat, an ascetic taught me how to plant citrus.
"See," he said, "it's just like your life—bitter and astringent, but at least it keeps going. "

In the Fallen Valley, we managed to communicate with the Lizards without a single word.
Thanks to the guides' well-planned escape routes, I learned to reflect on life while running for it.

While rushing to buy souvenirs on the Transport Station Market, I unexpectedly won second prize in the lottery— a sturdy cotton coat!
All the miners around looked at me with envy, as if I'd won some priceless treasure.

At the Oracle Plaza, I heard the Sacred Echo alongside the other Pilgrims!
The guides said it was just the wind whistling through ancient stone hollows, but to me, it felt real!
I swear it was saying: "Stop staring. You still have thirty-seven parameters left to adjust! "
At that moment, tears welled in my eyes...
I suddenly understood how important my work truly was! There are actually beings out there who care about what I do!

When I returned to Asterleeds, my coworkers said I looked like a different person.
"Ismark! That numb look in your eyes is gone. Now there's only... um... a kind of post-trauma positivity! "

So here I, Ismark, solemnly recommend the Pilgrimage to Bahamar to everyone! It made me feel reborn!

1031281.ReadingBookDes: Every unexpected event occurs precisely at the moment when no one expected it to happen.

1031282.BookName: Volume III: Lingering Shadows and Warnings
1031282.ReadingBookDes:
Although the name of Witch Hruga has gradually faded from memory since her sealing by the Creed, the threat of the Igdias has never truly vanished. Hruga's followers remain active in the shadows, searching ceaselessly for the remnants of her power and attempting to break the seal to welcome their master's return.
During the Asterleeds Independence War in Year 600 of the Alician calendar, cracks once appeared in Hruga's seal. At that time, the ​Void Engram​ once again spread across every corner of the Continent of Magna, becoming an ever-present gloom over people's hearts. With a common enemy looming, humanity united as never before under the mediation of the Creed, ultimately suppressing Hruga once again. The Creed then stepped forward to repair her seal again.

Today, the Illusory Bloom has erupted across the highlands once more, and the Illusory Plague again threaten the people living there. Rumors suggest that the followers of Hruga—those who previously spread disaster in Asterleeds—may have already fled to the highlands. The connection between the two cannot be ignored.
All of this warns us humans that we must put aside our hatred and disputes, remain vigilant against the remnants of the Igdias, and beware Witch Hruga!

1031283.BookName: New Approaches to Post-Plague Intervention III
1031283.ReadingBookDes:
III. The Kanamia Tribe's Shared Dream


The Kanamians have conducted extensive research on dreams. As far as I know, they can use a dream-entering medium called Ancestral Spores to enter another person's dream—and even expel the impurities that dwell within it. For this reason, the Kanamians believe that dreams are more real than reality itself... Though these accounts may be intertwined with elements of their ancestral spirit beliefs, the key point is that they have truly discovered a method to intervene in another's mind. Observations show that those who share a dream can reproduce its events with unfailing precision. This indicates that they do indeed enter the dreams of others and influence their thoughts.

The Kanamians have endured the trauma of war and suffered the ravages of the Void Corruption. For a people who place exceptional importance on the spiritual world, such inner wounds are no less devastating than the Illusory Plague. Yet through the use of Ancestral Spores, they have genuinely achieved shared dreaming, and with their own methods of banishing nightmares healed those wounds.

I was fortunate enough to experience a shared dream once, a ritual the Kanamians call the "Weaving of Dreams." The things that appeared within the dream all had clear counterparts in reality, yet in the dream they were grotesque, twisted into all manner of mutations... It was as if the dream were plainly telling us: this is the truest reflection of the trauma within.

1031284.ReadingBookDes:
To survive in the mines, you must strictly follow these rules:

Rule 1: If you're working and suddenly a pebble flies from behind you, do not turn around! Do not turn around! Do not turn around!

Rule 2: If an extra shadow of yourself appears under the searchlight, do not run. Hold your breath immediately.

Rule 3: If you see a minecart moving on its own along the tracks and glowing red, do not approach it, and never look directly inside the carriage!

Rule 4: If a miner's pickaxe suddenly lifts into the air on its own, step aside instantly and give up your digging spot.

Rule 5: If you hear dripping sounds coming from within the rock wall, whistle a full miner's tune immediately. Do not let the dripping sync with your heartbeat.

Rule 6: If you're alone and hear someone clearly call your full name, check your ID tag at once and confirm your name.

Final Rule: Keep this in mind that you always descend into the mines alone. If you suddenly hear someone speak to you, no matter what they ask, no matter how familiar the voice sounds, do not answer! Keep your eyes straight ahead and continue mining until the shift-change bell rings.

Please keep these rules in mind, and good luck—If anything goes wrong, check whether your shadow is still following you normally...

1031285.BookName: The One True Theory of Everything XXXVI
1031285.ReadingBookDes:
Doing business is simple: A deal isn't done until it's done.
And once it's done, it's done.

1031286.BookName: New Approaches to Post-Plague Intervention IV
1031286.ReadingBookDes:
IV. The Possibility of Shared-Dreaming Therapy


So what, then, is the method for healing such trauma? The answer seems obvious: within the shared dream, you must defeat these monsters—much like adventurers do in the real world. And astonishingly, after slaying these nightmare creatures, the people truly feel healed. Their eyes clear, their spirits brighten, as though their hearts have genuinely been purified.

Moreover, the Kanamians use this method not to heal one or two individuals, but entire groups—nearly every member of the tribe has undergone this shared-dreaming ritual.

This leads me to a bold idea: If we were to introduce this shared-dreaming therapy to highland residents suffering from the Illusory Plague's aftereffects, could it truly work? Or perhaps... what exactly would appear in the victims' dreams?
I believe it's worth attempting. The difficulty may not lie in guiding the victims into dreaming, but in obtaining the tools for shared dreaming. The Kanamians possess a rare type of buds used specifically for shared dreaming, but its quantity is extremely limited, and they employ it only during major ceremonies.

In the end, as I've said before, this is merely an attempt—a suggestion meant to point toward a possible direction. For lives on the highlands, still tormented by the lingering effects of the Illusory Plague, even the faintest hope is worth pursuing.

1031287.ReadingBookDes:
To my dear Marcel,

It has been a long time since I last wrote to you, and I'm not even sure if this letter will ever reach you... After all, the Blackstone Legion's surveillance grows stricter by the day.
Still, I must write. If there is even the slightest chance, it's worth trying.
Life down in the mines isn't good, but I suppose it isn't utterly unbearable either. At least the canteen serves meatballs once a week—though they're as hard as rocks, and the soup is so thin it might as well be rinse water from the cooking pot.

The Squad is as strict as ever. Their faces all look like they were carved from the same mold... No—each of them truly feels like a copy of the same template: identical boots, identical faces, identical whips. Even their footsteps have the same rhythm. Black boots striking stone—clack, clack, clack.

These days, even wiping sweat earns us the lash. It's as if we're not people, just pickaxes that move on their own. Starsoul Flasks are almost nowhere to be found, and every day someone collapses... yet no one ever cares.
Thinking about it carefully, I realize it has been a long time since I last saw Commander Klaus' stern face. He used to frown a lot, yes, but at least he followed some rules—he made sure we got medicine, and he distributed Starsoul Flasks regularly.
Now there isn't a single proper officer left in charge—just a bunch of loudmouths. One of them, named Carl, makes the loudest footsteps of all. He struts around arrogantly, caring only about production and never about our well-being. He loves dressing in black—black boots, black clothes, a black whip. I suspect even his heart is black.
Sometimes I can't help but wonder: Have even the stones down here been stained by the blackness of their boots?

I hope this letter reaches you. Don't write back—you know... the way here shifts quickly. All I wish is that I can live long enough to return to the surface, and that the sunlight up there is still the way I remember it.

Your old friend
From Sislesa Mine, Pit 1

1031288.ReadingBookDes:
Guess what? That guy Reiner came by again the other day! Remember the officious clerk I told you about last time? The one who talks all high and mighty? That guy was groveling in front of Reiner... his face practically twisted like a pug! Hahahaha!

But that's not the point. I was hiding nearby and overheard Reiner asking him for "waste," and saying something about consequences if he didn't hand it over. I didn't catch the last part clearly because just then a rat scurried past me... nearly giving me a heart attack! After Reiner said that, the clerk's face suddenly went pale, like he'd eaten rat poison!
Ah, now I finally get it—why people at the Transport Station have been muttering about picking up "waste" every day. Seems like it's some kind of treasure... I don't think this "waste" is that simple!
I figure it's probably the slag from my side being sent back to your end. I couldn't understand before why the ore was sent back underground after rough processing... now it makes sense!
Brother, your place is close to the mine. If you want to make some money, check around—see if there's any "waste"? There's bound to be plenty... If we can get some, we'll grab it, then run!
Run far away, never come back to this cursed highlands!
I'll send word when the coast is clear. Watch your back!


Your Brother

1031289.ReadingBookDes: (This magazine contains practical tips on rock identification and tunnel shoring, but it also holds fables written in mining slang, each with a hidden message of defiance. In its most secret corners, a few hastily scribbled pages track the destination of "waste" and the patrol routes of the "black boots.")

1031290.BookName: Shocking! Captain Reiner's New Boots Stolen by a Mine Rat!
1031290.ReadingBookDes:
Attention all miners! Captain Reiner's boots (the Type 31 Standard Officer Boots model) went missing during his inspection of Mine Pit No. 1. All miners are to begin searching for them at once!
These boots, of exquisite craftsmanship and distinguished style, are a symbol of Captain Reiner's commitment, and the very foundation of his sure-footedness in the treacherous mine tunnels.
An analysis of the scene indicates the captain was on-site in Mine Pit No. 1, inspecting the mining progress. Yet, a band of lawless mine rats, seizing the opportunity as Captain Reiner removed his boots to cool off, conspired to drag one of these dignified military boots away into the shadows.
This act is nothing less than a flagrant provocation against the Squad! Captain Reiner has always taken exceptional care of his boots, refusing to replace them even once since he began his post in the mines! And now, that noble boot is forced to share its space with these vile rats... Every moment we delay is a further trial on the rats' feeble bodies and minds.
In light of this, we, the mining community, must also take on the responsibility of recovering the boot. Whoever returns it shall be rewarded with ten canteen meatballs. Those who provide useful information shall receive a reward of one to five meatballs, depending on the lead!

1031291.ReadingBookDes:
IV. Conclusion: Boundary Marker of the Earth
By examining the two prevailing hypotheses, we can arrive at a partial consensus: The Needle Rock formations are characteristically sharp and jutting, indicating they are the result of external stimuli. By further identifying points of agreement and isolating disagreements, we can begin to investigate their true cause: The main point of divergence between these two theories is the origin of the energy involved. Yet, regardless of whether we consider the Pillar of Divinity or the witch Hruga, both are undeniably of unnatural creation.

Thus, we are forced to confront a conclusion as pointed as the Needle Rock formations themselves—that they are, perhaps, a form of immunological rejection by the highland terrain.

This immunological rejection is likely not from any single event, but from a great many such events that have inflicted excessive devastation upon the Bahamar Highlands in ages past: Xeno Engram, war, the Divine Ruins, and even more calamities lost to our knowledge. These calamities have surpassed nature's ability to heal, overwhelming the world's capacity to endure, and ultimately causing the land of the highlands to develop this kind of rejection mechanism.

Perhaps the warning carried by the Needle Rock is the very same message the scar-like ruins across the highlands are trying to convey. What is past is gone, and there is little to be gained by dwelling on it. We can only hope that in the years to come, each time we are struck with awe by their form, we will use them as a boundary marker—a reason to reflect upon and remember the past.

1031292.BookName: The One True Theory of Everything XLVIII
1031292.ReadingBookDes: The whole point of eating is to clean your plate.

1031293.ReadingBookDes:
These rocks have voices, you know. You learn to hear them after you've been mining long enough. If you don't believe it, just go ask old Taylor.
You hit it with your pick, and it goes clink-clank, clink-clank... Now that's some fine ore! Still, it's lackin' a certain ring to it. Ore like this is just stubborn and hard, so you can't force your way through. When you're dealing with this kind of ore, us miners know to take it easy. Shoot the breeze, trade some stories... or just sit back and wipe the sweat from your brow. Nobody's going to say a word. This is how you have to handle ore this rigid. If you're too tense, you'll snap the head of your pickaxe. It's that simple. A broken tool is one thing, but injuring a fellow miner is another matter entirely.
Some ore trembles even when you don't strike it. *Thrum... thrum... thrum.* The sound draws closer—unhurried, relentless. It has the certainty of a death knell. That sound tells you it's prime ore, the highest quality there is. You can't be careless with this ore. You have to be on high alert, swallow any words you were about to say, and even if you break a leg, prop yourself up on the other and keep swinging until the whole mine rings with the sound. Don't look where you shouldn't look, and don't ask what you shouldn't ask. Otherwise, by the time that sound is in your ear, you'll be seeing red for sure, unable to sit or stand... Just listen to the veteran miners. You won't go wrong.

1031294.ReadingBookDes:
Everyone's been to the transfer zone, right? There's a big one there! A Rock Serpent! But don't worry, the black-booted guards have a way with that Rock Serpent. The isolation gate comes down, the sleeping gas sprays, and suddenly you're on a different side of the fence—not you from the serpent, but the fast from the slow... So keep your eyes on those black boots. The moment they start to fall back, you follow! Even if you have to grab them by the belt, you squeeze through that isolation gate with them.
Some of the workers can't handle the pressure. They get picked to go and start shaking like a leaf in the wind. Can't even swing a pickaxe straight. Then the black boots catch 'em, and they get an earful... It's useless. Anyone who works in this pit will get sent there one day. It's a blessing! I heard the food in the transfer zone even comes with a few extra meatballs. You absolutely have to save those. In an emergency, if you pick your moment and hurl them at the Rock Serpent, you'll leave a real dent!

1031295.ReadingBookDes:
A smart miner is always good at planning routes. Only by mastering this skill can you mine more effectively in this district and hope to walk out of the pits alive one day.

First is reading the map. It's an essential skill to learn the direction of the known "ore veins." These routes have already been meticulously charted by other workers. Give them a little something—half a piece of dried meat, a few pages from a magazine... and they'll be happy to share with you. Planning your own efficient mining routes based on the paths of these "ore veins" is the key to becoming a veteran miner.

Next is planning. Find the pattern—always choose a path that doesn't intersect with the main "ore vein" routes. If you absolutely must cross, calculate the timing down to the second, and make sure you get through quickly during a gap in the "ore vein's" flow.

Lastly, remember the principle—mining is a miner's duty, but your body is more important. You have to be alive to mine. It's not smart to let your body collide violently with an "ore vein."
A good miner puts their own safety first. Before you make any decision, think about your family. Think about the sun that's about to rise.

1031296.ReadingBookDes:
Dearest Mom and Dad,

Life down in the mines is getting by. The Squad is as serious as ever. Everyone wears a grim expression. Carl said it's an "iron mask" issued by the higher-ups, and that wearing it is for my own good. I didn't understand at first, but after I saw what they did to the miners... I get it now.
If there's anything good to say about it down here, it's probably the stability of the daily routine. But that's not the whole story. A while ago, something seemed to happen in Mine No. 1. I heard yelling and the sounds of a fight. Could a Rock Serpent have gotten over there? Unfortunately, I was changing shifts that day, so I wasn't on duty there. I didn't see what happened.
But ever since then, the atmosphere seems to have gotten even colder. Carl's like a different person. He won't say a word, no matter what I ask him. But that's normal, too. After all, this is the Sislesa Mine. No one dares to say a single unnecessary word, and laughter is even more out of place.
It's just that sometimes, when I look into the depths of the mine, I can't help but wonder: in these bottomless mine tunnels, who really benefits? Who's happy here?
I don't really understand. I just know I have to wear this iron mask for another three months. In three months, I'll be home safe. Everything will be all right then.

I hope you are both well. Please don't worry about me.
— Your loving son, Allan

1031297.ReadingBookDes:
The mine is suddenly under lockdown. They say some big shot has arrived! Mathis said not to worry, that the investigation won't reach us. He says the person is just here to monitor mining progress, and that it's an annual visit.
But when I went to relieve myself last night, I actually stumbled upon the big shot talking secretly with the manager in a corner! I quickly hid myself and overheard them talking about how "the Crimson Marrow yield has decreased again," "the Drava Royal Institute's Furnace Legacy is almost grinding to a halt," and "the Grand Duke is furious"... It all sounded very bad. The manager could only nod and bow, constantly forcing a smile.
Then the big shot leaned closer and said a few more words... and the manager's expression immediately changed! Tsk, tsk... It's still chilling to think about now. I'm afraid that face will be a staple in my nightmares.

After that, I don't even remember how I got back to my bunk. I just remember being completely numb, lying on my bed like a corpse, all sleepiness gone.
Will the big shot just let this slide? Will the manager think we've been negligent in our supervision? Or could it be... that THING has finally been discovered by the higher-ups, so they sent someone to investigate?
*Sigh* I can't believe Mathis can sleep through this. I'll have to question him thoroughly when he wakes up and pry some truth out of him.

1031298.BookName: The Art of Absolute Tongue IX
1031298.ReadingBookDes:
The key to this problem is to identify the key issue.
As long as the crucial issue is resolved, the problem will solve itself.

1031299.ReadingBookDes:
For Miss Valeria's eyes only:
Ahhhhh... Dearest Miss Valeria, I have finally mustered the courage to write to you again! Please forgive my messy handwriting, for the mere thought of you fills me with an excitement I cannot contain!
You replied to my last letter saying I was too talkative and you had no time for idle chatter, and I have been silent for a long time since... but this letter is definitely not idle chatter! It is because I have truly discovered a major problem!
It's... it's just that the Illusory Blooms have erupted on a massive scale across the Bahamar Highlands once more. Lallipar was the first to be hit, and many have fallen victim to the Illusory Plague... Many scholars and doctors have gone to the highlands to help, but adventurers are conspicuously absent! The strength of the Creed and the Asterleeds Defense Corps alone is not enough to completely eradicate the Illusory Blight here!
Perhaps the people here are too busy dealing with the Illusory Plague to request aid from the Pioneer Bureau, or perhaps the Pioneer Bureau has yet to receive a formal report, and the information is simply delayed. But the disaster will not wait. New victims appear every single day!
In any case, Miss Valeria, you said last time, "Do not write to me unless it is on official business, and do not come to the Pioneer Bureau." This is indeed an official matter! At present, the Illusory Blight in the highlands remains severe. Please dispatch adventurer reinforcements!
As for compensation, I will come to the Pioneer Bureau to discuss the details with you in person!


Wilp
Lallipar

P.S. I understand your time is precious, so I have enclosed with this letter a signed statement of the situation from the village chief and a copy of the aid request from the Creed's local garrison. Please review them. The situation is extremely urgent!

1031318.ReadingBookDes:
Dearest Anna,
You've never seen a forest like it! The trees are so tall they seem to tear the sky open, and the fog is so thick it clings to your face like cream. The Pioneer Bureau calls it the Slumberdream Valley. Me... I think it's more like a place that just swallows people's sleep.
You'll definitely laugh—I actually dozed off while I was lost in there! When I woke up, I was covered in a cold sweat. I'd just dreamed that the tree roots were moving, as if they were about to entangle me.
But don't worry, I got out of there with a cool head and a bit of luck. It's just that the feeling of the nightmare seems to stick in my head even after waking up. I can't shake it off.
Ah, speaking of which, I have to admit... I haven't dared to tell anyone else about this. I'm afraid they'd laugh at me for being a coward.
You'd better not laugh at me. By the way, if I can really overcome all this, that counts as part of my training as an adventurer, right?

Your brother,
Federico, who's trying to be more reliable

1031319.ReadingBookDes:
To my dearest Mom,
I must tell you about a rather unpleasant experience I had (but don't worry, I'm all right now).
Recently, we were sent on a mission to a place called the Slumberdream Valley. The fog is thick there, and it's easy to lose your bearings. The strangest thing is... when you fall asleep there, your dreams feel exceptionally real.
I dreamed I was back home, but the house was empty. Only the bowls on the dining table were still steaming. I knew it wasn't real, but in the dream, I was desperately searching for you and Anna. I was still shaking when I woke up.

I'm starting to wonder if I'm really cut out for this kind of adventuring.

I'm actually much better now. I just wanted you to know that I haven't forgotten home, and I haven't forgotten your lamb and tomato stew.

Your son,
Federico, who is always trying to grow

1031320.ReadingBookDes:
To Anna:
(This entire section is crossed out) I want to tell you about the dream I had—I saw you, but you kept walking away from me, your back turned. No matter how I chased you, I couldn't catch up. The shadows of the trees fell like curtains, layer after layer, separating me from you.
(A scribbled note on the side: This part is too weird, don't write it.)
On a serious note, I'm actually doing okay in the Slumberdream Valley. The mission is going quite smoothly. It's just that the fog is so thick, it easily makes you hallucinate. But then again, your brother isn't one to panic in a forest—I'm very calm.
Ah, but sometimes, the fog is really annoying. You know, like that night when we were kids and had a fight, and you insisted on turning off the light. Haha, I still feel angry when I think about it now.
I'm really fine, Anna. You don't need to worry about me—nightmares and all, even if they come, they can't stop me from moving forward.

(The letter stops here, seemingly put aside for the time being.)

1031321.ReadingBookDes:
Hey, little brother,
You said you couldn't catch up to me in your dream? Hahaha, that sounds just like you. You're always half a step behind, shouting for me to wait for you.
But in all seriousness, that fog and those strange nightmares, they sound a bit scary. But I'm not worried about you at all. Your handwriting is still steady in your letter, which means you're fine.
Even if you feel "insignificant," in my eyes you're the most amazing brother there is. It's okay if you can't catch me in a nightmare. In reality, you're catching up to your own dreams, step by step.
So, cheer up! Next time you see Lady Airona, remember to actually go talk to her, and don't just stare from afar. Then—I'll be waiting for that autograph and all the details of the story!

Your ever-supportive sister,
Anna

1031325.ReadingBookDes:
I hear footsteps in the night,
but no one draws near.
In the howling wind, I see firelight,
but no fire warms me.

I reach out my hand and touch a stone wall.
The stone wall cracks, revealing an eye.
It watches me, like a mirror,
yet it doesn't show me myself.

1031326.ReadingBookDes:
They say, "Sleep now."
"Close your eyes, and you can go home."
But as soon as I fall asleep,
the path is replaced by countless overlapping doors.

I push open a door, and there is still a door.
I call out familiar names,
and only the wind answers me:
You are not here, you have not returned, you do not wake.

1031327.ReadingBookDes:
I'd bet my life that no one on this entire continent is more miserable than I am.
I work like an animal all day, and at night, I still have to haggle with my own dreams.
In my dream, my stall is piled high with goods, all dazzling and shiny, but nobody's buying.
They just crowd around and look, saying, "None of this is real." Then, in the blink of an eye, all the goods are gone, leaving me naked behind the stall.
...I hate dreaming. It's worse than getting haggled down.

1031328.ReadingBookDes:
First, apply a base coat for the background, using a deep gray-blue. It can't be too dark.
The tree trunks should be elongated slightly. Don't draw them straight. They look more natural if they're crooked...
First, establish the lines with a hard pen, then soften the edges with a soft brush.
For the fog, don't use white directly. Mix gray and white, and brush it on lightly in a thin layer.
Remember to leave a blank space in the middle. The floating light will be painted there later.

1031329.ReadingBookDes:
The points of light must be painted in layers!
First, apply a transparent layer of pale yellow, then add brighter white dots on top.
The placement can't be too orderly, or it will look fake... It must be randomized!
Feather the edges with a dry brush, dragging the points of light to create a slight blur.
Finally, fill the gaps with cool colors, and the sparkling effect will emerge.

1031330.ReadingBookDes:
The stones should be outlined with hard lines, then blocked in with cool blue and gray tones.
The cracks in the center should be carved out with a knife, and then filled in with thin, bright blue lines!
The reflections on the surface must be preserved. Use a clean brush dipped in pure water to wipe away the pigment.
Don't paint it as a solid... It needs to breathe. This can be expressed through layered colors and empty spaces.
The shadows must remain clean, not muddied with the background.

1031331.ReadingBookDes:
Okay, the Light Cocoon must be placed right in the center.
For the base color, first mix transparent red and yellow, then apply a touch of blue to the outer ring.
The edge of the cocoon should not be traced with a brush... it should be gently dabbed on with a sponge.
The bright spots inside should be a bit larger and more chaotic than the surrounding light specks to appear natural.
Finally, enclose it in dark colors to build a sense of pressure, which will make the Light Cocoon pop!

1031332.ReadingBookDes:
Pay attention to the overall composition: top-heavy, light at the bottom.
The branches should extend from both sides, pulling the viewer's eye toward the center.
The points of light must gradually decrease from left to right to create a sense of direction.
The stone should be placed in the bottom right corner to give the painting weight. Otherwise, it will feel like it's floating.
Don't paint the full figure... Just leave a blurry silhouette on the left to establish scale.

1031333.ReadingBookDes:
Today, I finally finished this painting.
The layers of fog turned out better than I expected, especially the soft-focus effect in the top-right corner. It's almost identical to the sights I saw in the Slumberdream Valley.
The Light Cocoon's position is slightly off, but the overall composition is still balanced. The distribution of the light specks is quite natural, avoiding the lifelessness I was most afraid of. Bless the Bapharian Divines! This is truly fantastic!
The effect of carving the cracks in the stone with a knife is much more realistic than my previous attempts with brushstrokes. That was a good discovery.
The only thing I'm not satisfied with is the figure's silhouette. The edge transition is too hard, making it look a bit abrupt, but I don't want to change it anymore.

I know this painting doesn't record reality, but an illusion. But I still want to keep it.
It frightens me, and it fascinates me. After finishing it, I was even somewhat reluctant to put down my brush.

I've decided to name it—Prison of Floating Light.

A tooth that escaped someone's mouth

1031336.ReadingBookDes:

Orange Berry Trio
Pink Orange Quintet
Black Banana Septet

1031337.ReadingBookDes:

7
8

The Bapharian Divines
Humans

1031339.ReadingBookDes:

Where does the Frost Mage's ability to control the element of ice come from?
Talent
It's magic! Magic!
A Bapharian Legacy

A Bapharian Legacy

1031340.ReadingBookDes:

Denvel
Taltraud
You wretched worms

Denvel

1031341.ReadingBookDes:

Dual swords
A staff

The Muku Warrior uses a specially modified giant hammer.

1031342.ReadingBookDes:

Jerrad
Lamond

1031343.ReadingBookDes:

An echo
A shadow
Smoke

A shadow
