Congratulations! You've completed all of this year's Renewal Festival riddles.
May the Renewal Light illuminate your path in the year ahead.
—Light may fade, but the moments we remember endure.

1031353.ReadingBookDes:
...Webber Industry, founded by the legendary artisan of the same name, is a massive industrial organization that designed and built the world-changing Asterleeds energy network.
Headquartered in Byrnhald, its core business covers Legacy research and modification, mechanical design and production, and various cutting-edge technology R&D projects.
Given the company's massive scale and industrial nature, the top brass of Webber Industry holds significant influence in Byrnhald's political arena.
It is worth noting that Webber Industry has had a long-standing tense relationship with the Byrnhald Diocese, a relationship that has played a part in the political unrest that Byrnhald faces as it seeks to separate church and state affairs.
The two sides are wary of each other, stubbornly refusing to give up any ground as they desperately try to find leverage to use against one another, all in the hope of manufacturing an opportunity to drive the opposing party into a corner.

1031354.ReadingBookDes:
Monday
By my count, it's been over half a month since I left the Pillar of Divinity, and I'm still not used to wearing ordinary clothes.
They're loose and baggy, completely lacking the solid, rigid feel of the Creed uniform.

Tuesday
That kid Seon is quite handy on Creed missions, but in everyday life—well, he's all but guaranteed to mess things up.
I asked him to fetch me some water, and he made me wait a whole two hours. When I asked him why, he said the water source here is dirty and causes hallucinations.
He even insisted he saw a school of fish swimming in a bizarre vortex in the water... Even as angry as I was, I couldn't help but laugh.

Wednesday
The artisans and alchemists are at it again. The arguments are absolutely laughable, and they're so loud I could hear them clearly from the nearby woods.
They're both camped right next to the same ruins, but they're acting like they have a blood feud.
If you ask me, the leaders of both sides need to come to the Creed and learn what it means to be open-minded.

Thursday
I have no idea what's wrong with the weather at these ruins. There's never even been a breath's worth of wind. It's almost as if the weather here never changes.
The clouds haven't seemed to move at all either, and the angle of the sunlight has barely shifted.
Perhaps the fact that our intended target hasn't arrived is affecting my mood, but the state of deadlock we're in is truly making me anxious.

Friday
Today, I asked that kid Seon to clean out the ashes from the campfire. He treated it as if I'd asked him to search and arrest someone, meticulously digging through every handful of ash he swept out.
He turned the camp into a smoky, dusty mess, and I nearly choked from coughing.
When I asked him why, he said he saw the ashes twitch a few times and was worried a monster was hiding inside.
Impulsively, I retorted that maybe it was the person drawing those vortex patterns, and that he'd better let them finish before he arrested them, so we'd have evidence.
I never imagined he'd freeze up like he did, before whimpering out, "...I really did see it."
Well, I guess at least he's developing a sense of humor.

1031355.BookName: "Blueprints and Models: Features of Artificial Geometry"
1031355.ReadingBookDes:
...When novice artisan crafters first try their hand at furniture design, they often struggle to grasp the difference between natural patterns and artificial shapes.
They painstakingly draw crests and patterns to overlay on their crafts, expecting them to be the finishing touch, only to make fools of themselves by accidentally creating artificial geometric shapes that look like equipment blueprints.

Ultimately, this is because they confuse naturally grown textures with shapes drawn for a specific purpose.
Crafting furniture and designing equipment are two different things: the lines on equipment often serve a practical purpose, while the patterns on furniture mostly serve an aesthetic function.
To make your patterns look more natural rather than like equipment, keep the following points in mind:

1. Avoid setting a purpose first.
Artificially designed shapes often have a clear purpose: you think of a shape first, then press it into the medium, so it naturally looks "carved in." Conversely, natural patterns seem to grow along with the material and structure.

2. Avoid pursuing consistency.
During your apprenticeship, mentors often teach you to make things symmetrical, neat, and easy to repeat. This is a useful principle for equipment, but when applied to decorations, it can easily cause them to become monotonous and rigid.
Natural patterns can approach geometry, of course, but their similarity comes from underlying rules rather than exact duplication; upon closer inspection, there are always slight differences.

3. Avoid making the edges too sharp.
The boundaries of natural textures are often transitional, scattered, worn, or covered, while artificially drawn edges tend to be clear, gathered, and truncated. The more an edge looks like a knife cut, the more unnatural it appears.

4. Avoid forcing hierarchical obedience.
Equipment graphics often emphasize an order of primary structure, secondary structure, and fine structure, with details serving the primary structure. The more you look at them, the more they look like a blueprint. Natural patterns are more prone to local, independent growth, without strictly requiring every layer to take orders from a center. The more obsessed you are with hierarchical order, the more mechanical the work will feel, pushing you further away from natural textures.

5. Trust your first intuition.
If a certain shape makes you feel unnatural, uncomfortable, or like it was carved out at first glance, it's probably not you overthinking it. Often, a key detail (symmetry, edge, repetition, or position) is just too clean.

Finally, do not overemphasize the importance of the pattern. The furniture is the purpose, and the pattern is merely the carrier.
But do not underestimate the danger of patterns either. If a certain pattern appears repeatedly across different materials, scales, and scenes,
and always appears in the most informative position, then it can be easily interpreted as a deliberately inscribed mark rather than a natural accident.

1031356.ReadingBookDes:
...The creatures in these ruins feel exceptionally smart.
When I went out to gather herbs, I casually looked up and saw a flock of birds circling in a spiral, so orderly it looked as if someone was directing them.

At that moment, I suddenly remembered something Clement had said: all things in this world think and speak. Mountains, rivers, lakes, and seas are constantly singing, we just cannot hear them.
He even gave a bizarre example, saying that a flock of thirty-one sheep and a flock of thirty sheep are two different entities; what they think and say are completely different.

He also told me he'd once seen foxen circling something, and as they circled, they formed a very regular pattern.
At the time, I just thought he was letting his imagination run wild again, but now... I think he would be very interested in everything happening here.

Unfortunately, he went to the valley for research.
When things wrap up here, I must go find him and tell him everything that's happened. Maybe he really can give me an explanation.
Yeah, I think I'll do that.

...

That strange dream again.
In the dream, I heard a lot of noise outside, so I pushed the door open to look and found a traveling troupe performing in the ruins, with everyone laughing.
Then, a Fagaro approached, leaned in very close, and said something vicious to me—

I woke up with a start.
I was so scared, I forgot what he actually said.
But I clearly remember: on their foreheads was printed a terrifying spiral, exactly the same as the spiral the flock of birds had formed during the day.

1031357.ReadingBookDes:
Unlike the artisans, alchemists never shy away from the unknown when pondering problems.
They always leave an empty slot in their formulas specifically for that inexplicable yet necessary unknown factor involved in a given reaction. The alchemists refer to this type of unknown variable as a catalyst.

The same catalyst, when mixed with different materials, produces countless subtle variations:
sometimes it has a catalyzing effect, sometimes it actually promotes restoration, and sometimes it even fundamentally changes a product's crystallized form.
Alchemists never seek to explain the reasons behind this; they believe that the unknown element, the reaction, and the materials used are all part of a greater, holistic process,
and this process itself is one of their golden rules: the formula.

All potions in alchemy are derived through formulas. They even believe that the entire world is one giant formula, and the constantly changing present is the unknown within that formula.
It's said the artisans laughed aloud when they heard this.
In their eyes, there are no unknowns in the world; even if there are, they will eventually become known in the future.
One artisan jokingly asked if alchemists also need to use a formula when they relieve themselves, to mitigate the risk of constipation.

From a theoretical standpoint, I think both sides are equally matched—but when it comes to tact, the artisans are definitely lacking.

1031358.ReadingBookDes:
While exploring the ruins today, I unexpectedly ran into a master painter!

She was dressed quite plainly and would be completely unnoticeable in a crowd, but you could tell at a glance that she had true skill. She wasn't just casually sketching.
Seeing her so focused, I was too embarrassed to strike up a conversation, so I stood off to the side and quietly watched.

She seemed fond of painting landscapes. Each scene wasn't just a one-and-done thing for her; she made draft after draft first, as if confirming the lines from a certain angle until she was satisfied.

Today she was painting a section of a wall in the ruins. The wall looked like a Bapharian Legacy, yet it had grown together with the natural rock face next to it.
It's actually quite common in these ruins, but she painted it with extreme care.
Every crease and peeling spot on the wall was rendered faithfully stroke by stroke—she didn't even miss the mottled mark in the corner.

I watched for a while, then left because I got hungry.
But for some reason, while watching her paint, time seemed to freeze, and I felt almost as if my heart had been cleansed.
I hope I run into her again next time.

1031359.ReadingBookDes:
I'm so excited today, my heart is pounding! Why? Because I met that painter again!

This time she wasn't working on a landscape, but a mechanical structure. I leaned in for a closer look... it looked like a chicken with a clockwork mechanism in its belly!
What's even stranger is that she was as familiar with mechanical structures as an artisan. The springs and gears were drawn in extreme detail, with clean and crisp lines.
She even drew a magnified view of the local details; on the inside of the spring, there was a beautiful spiral mark printed.
When you really looked at it, it didn't seem like a casual sketch. I'd say something more like a blueprint of some sort. Perhaps drawing blueprints is her idea of fun?

I can't help but feel a bit put out. I guess it really is a good thing to learn new things.
I mean, it seems like you've got to even know a bit of mechanical design to be a painter nowadays, and they say you have to study anatomy to draw the human body...
And then you've got me, who goes out for an adventure and ends up spraining an ankle. I'm so useless!

1031360.ReadingBookDes:
I actually spoke with the painter lady yesterday!
At first, I just wanted to watch her paint a bit. I'd lost my food sack, so I was a bit out of sorts. I figured watching her work might cheer me up.

I never thought that as soon as I approached, she'd smile at me and ask what I thought of her painting.
I mean, what could I say, really? She had already become like the silvery moonlight that shines on my windowsill at night—there weren't enough words to describe how good she was!
Still, I used all the vocabulary I'd learned over the course of my life to praise her, even to the point where it got a bit sappy... but she just smiled faintly, as if she was already used to it.

Then she handed me a painting and said, "Open it when you get home."
The painting was already rolled up and placed next to her easel, almost as if it had been prepared especially for me.
I was extremely flattered and even tried to stutter out my thanks.

But when I got home and unrolled the painting, I was startled.
By Bapharia! What is this on the painting? It looked like a massive, dark crystal.
The patterns on the surface of the crystal were so complex they made my scalp tingle, intertwining and crisscrossing. At first glance, it looked like a tangled mess...
But on further inspection, it seemed as if it was being guided by some force, naturally falling into place at some points, and finally twisting into a triangular mark.

For some reason, looking at that shape made me extremely uncomfortable, as if it were a pupil staring at me.
I closed the painting almost instinctively, my palms drenched in sweat.

Early this morning, I rushed back to the ruins, wanting to find her and ask what this painting actually was.
But she had disappeared.
The spot where her easel stood was empty, as if no one had ever stood there painting.

1031361.ReadingBookDes:
People are saying that the lingering aftereffects of the Illusory Plague that broke out near Lallipar are causing trouble there again, interrupting a brief period of calm in the region.

Several villagers stated that over the past week, they have repeatedly had the same dream, in which they turned into a strange yellow-backed fox, constantly touching noses with other yellow-backed foxes in a pitch-black woodland area.
At first, it was just two or three, but later the numbers grew, forming a massive pack of the creatures.
Finally, they arrived at a moonlit lake, circling the water as if dancing a dance no one had taught them—almost as if forming a certain shape.
The entire scene was incredibly orderly, as if guided by the same thought.

What's even more bizarre is that the villagers claim certain characteristics of the foxes in the dreams were extremely similar to their own.
Their posture, gait—they even felt a sense of familiarity when one approached.
They suspect that this is not a simple nightmare, but rather some kind of shared dream.

Regardless of the true nature of the dreams, we urge all residents near Lallipar to avoid approaching woodland areas and lakes at night if they notice strange phenomena, and to remain vigilant against the Illusory Plague.

1031362.ReadingBookDes:
Some zoologists have proposed a different view regarding the claims that the Illusory Plague has struck Lallipar again.
Real-life yellow-backed foxes touch noses to exchange information. Not all creatures use verbal language to communicate, after all—scent is also a common medium.
Furthermore, since yellow-backed foxes appear in large numbers in the woodland areas not far from Lallipar, the villagers are most likely simply dreaming about what they see during the day. This, they argue, makes their dreams less than solid evidence that the Illusory Plague has made a comeback.

Upon hearing this, some busybodies immediately retorted that
even if what the scholars said was true, what kind of information would such a massive group of yellow-backed foxes be trying to convey?
That is the more unsettling part.

1031363.ReadingBookDes:
Recently, the Asterleeds Diocese delivered two precision Legacy devices codenamed "Mark 07" and "Light 04" to the Guild.
Mark 07 cuts materials very accurately, reducing the margin of error to its absolute limit.
Light 04, on the other hand, measures objects using light rays.
The precision of these two instruments has once again shattered the Guild's upper limits of accuracy—in fact, it practically redefines the word "limit."

Usually, such a delivery would have sparked a frenzy among the artisans, as measuring equipment is practically equivalent to a second eye for an artisan.
Unexpectedly, however, as of the writing of this article, the bookings for these instruments haven't even filled a single page.
The reason is not a lack of efficacy in the Legacy devices, but rather that the artisans' attention has been firmly captured by the uncertainty phenomena in the Bahamar Highlands.

Reports have it that two artisans were dispatched to ruins in the highlands to conduct basic measurements, aiming to archive wall heights, angles, and other foundational data.
However, they were surprised to find that measurements at the same location yielded random deviations, and these deviations did not follow any correctable pattern.
...At first, they simply assumed it was due to shaky hands, blurry vision, or moisture affecting their instruments. But after repeated verification and cross-measurement, the errors still could not be eliminated.

The two artisans nervously reported the matter, but were dismissed by the Guild as slacking off and making excuses. They were even ordered to take some time and reflect on their actions.
However, when the replacement artisans sent to measure again arrived at the exact same conclusion, the matter finally began to be handled formally.

Subsequently, measurement teams were rotated one after another, bringing with them increasingly precise instruments—but ultimately, they all failed.
These errors were finally presented to Dorothy, the Artisan Guild's Guildmaster. According to witnesses, she was so furious upon reading them that she nearly smashed the table to pieces.
Eventually, the uncertainty phenomena were internally acknowledged by the Guild, and a specialized survey team was stationed in the highlands soon after. However, as of now, progress remains extremely slow.

The Guild has placed high importance on this matter internally, and the calls to pit Mark 07 and Light 04 against the uncertainty phenomena are growing louder.
Before publishing this article, this author saw the Guild loading the two Legacy devices into vehicles borrowed from the garrison.

Perhaps, in the near future, we will witness with our own eyes whether the limits of measurement end with our instruments, or with the world itself.

1031364.ReadingBookDes:
The two famed precision measurement Legacy devices, codenamed "Mark 07" and "Light 04" by the Guild,
were recently transported to the highlands, officially kicking off the showdown against measurement errors.

The writer of this article is here to bring you firsthand coverage of the scene!

The artisan handling logistics, Marcel, transferred the energy modules for both instruments and performed initial calibrations.
Team leader Valerian designed a simple first experiment for Mark 07, tasking it with precisely cutting a piece of stone from the ruins according to a preset thickness.
However, after it bustled around for a while, the thickness of Mark 07's cut still was far off expectations.
A sharp-tongued intern standing nearby muttered that the instrument's cutting wasn't even as precise as if he used a chisel to make the cut himself.

So, Mark 07 admitted defeat. What about Light 04?

On the afternoon of the same day, the first experiment for Light 04 officially began, which also involved measuring the walls of the ruins.
Typically, this kind of measurement should have been completed almost instantly by Light 04.
However, a rare scene unfolded today. The measuring beams of Light 04 converged and scattered, sweeping back and forth across the walls of the ruins.
The readings continuously looped, yet could never lock onto a fixed measurement value.
It was very much like a highly nearsighted person looking for their glasses in the morning—but Light 04 eventually found its glasses.

After a bit of fumbling, the beam of Light 04 unsettlingly focused on a mottled mark in the corner of the wall, and then fell still. For a moment, no one on the scene made a sound.

Afterward, we interviewed that sharp-tongued intern, Julien.
Due to his disrespectful remarks in the morning, he was ordered off the afternoon's experiments by the team leader and assigned to organize records instead.
When we asked him what he thought of all this, Julien first looked around, then lowered his voice and said:
"They're wrong, even the more senior artisans among us. They shouldn't be trying to figure out how to measure everything accurately.
Because what if this is actually just a phenomenon we've never seen before? We might be something like a person who has never seen rain, and thus thinks the world is inherently dry.
This phenomenon has made us all into primitives... But I will figure out a way to unravel this mystery. I already have an idea."

Regardless, even though both instruments have suffered setbacks once again, the artisans' momentum remains strong. This clash of limits has only just begun. Keep an eye out for further news!

1031365.BookName: Letters Left Behind in Sunken Corridor
1031365.ReadingBookDes:
My old friend Juster,

Greetings!

Ever since the higher-ups launched that large-scale search operation, we've been scattered, separated by great distances.
Time truly has flown by. We used to stand guard together beneath the Pillar of Divinity, exchanging notes at dawn and dusk,
arguing over seemingly trivial doctrinal issues... Now, those days seem gone forever.
To be honest, I kind of miss that regularity. Even though every day was the same, perhaps even a bit mechanical, at least I was certain I was doing no wrong, and my heart was at peace.

But life recently has been truly bizarre. I constantly feel like I'm living half-awake in a dream...
Perhaps it has something to do with what the higher-ups want us to find. Yet, what exactly are they thinking? They send us out to search, but won't tell us what we are actually looking for.
They just keep telling us, "Go search and discover—the rewards will come to you..." Honestly, the biggest reward I've gotten has been strange looks from the people around me.

At first, people were happy to interact with us. They used to greet people like us with smiles, but it's different now.
They hide from us, avoid our gaze—even asking for directions feels like we're treading on some taboo.
It's as if the moment people like us get close, we'll immediately dig up the secrets hidden at the very bottom of their wardrobes.
It makes me start to question: what is the meaning of wearing this uniform every day?

Juster, my old friend, you know me well. I, Cedric, am a busybody and mischievous by nature. I didn't join this line of work to cultivate my character, but because I wanted to help people.
But this time... I truly feel a sense of powerlessness. It's just like that kid Boyce said: "The foundation beneath our feet is trembling."

I've done a lot of investigating in private, wanting to find out what exactly the higher-ups are looking for—even just the reason behind their sudden, extreme agitation.
They are tight-lipped, of course, but with a great deal of effort, I finally managed to catch a glimpse of the truth.
My friend, the implications behind this matter are vast—far too vast. Alone, I can't even begin to grasp the full picture...
I can only tell you three things for now: don't dig too deep, don't report anything, and don't trust anyone.

Finally, and most importantly, please come catch up at the Gloomy Depths on the ■■th of next month. I've invited Edreon, Elowen, and a few other old friends to join us.
We can talk late into the night and piece our information together into the truth.
I look forward to your reply, and to seeing you.
(Don't let Seon see this letter, and don't mention it to any of the guards.)

Cedric

1031366.BookName: Frequent Unusual Weather, Is the Illusory Plague Returning?
1031366.ReadingBookDes:
Thanks to the combined efforts of factions including the Pioneer Bureau and the Creed, initial steps have been taken to alleviate the Illusory Plague in the Bahamar Highlands, and the villagers there have been able to return to their normal lives.
Lallipar was even able to hold a grand celebration banquet.
At the banquet, a local villager presented hand-made gifts to the distinguished adventurers present, as if declaring to the world that the suffering was finally coming to an end.

However, a recent series of Engram Anomalies has forced people to turn their attention back to the aftermath.
Some villagers have recently reported to the Creed that they've noticed frequent, sudden changes in wind speed.
Stranger still, the wind appears to be carrying a sort of melody each time, like some sort of disjointed song...
"The sound of the wind is terrifying!
It's as if something suddenly swoops past you at high speed...
The wind took my hat along with it, but I couldn't see a soul nearby!" one villager described.

Another villager stated that he saw a strange phenomenon where the sky changed color.
"I was weeding near the village that day when I suddenly noticed the color of the grass looked a bit different.
I looked up, and bless my soul if the sky wasn't purple, like it had been dyed by Illusory Blooms!"

In addition, we have received multiple reports of strange birds being sighted, although the descriptions of the birds are inconsistent. Typically, the creatures are described as having three to nine wings and one to five legs.

The Creed is leaning toward classifying these instances as hallucinations. But the Illusory Blooms outside the village have long been eradicated, so where could they be coming from?
A High Priest who has long been involved in handling the Illusory Plague stated that everything in Regnus contains Engrams.
Normal Engrams can be infected by Xeno Engram Catalysts, transforming them into Xeno Engrams that can then cause hallucinations.

Currently, the Creed suspects that these Engram Anomalies are very likely due to an unexplained rise in Xeno Engram concentration. Although the cause has not yet been identified, it undoubtedly sounds the alarm for the highlands once again.

1031367.ReadingBookDes:
Energy issues have always been a chronic pain point for the Guild.
With the usage rate of Asterleeds Legacy devices climbing daily, the load on the Webber Energy Network has long exceeded its limits.
To maintain the stability of the network, the Guild had to enforce regulations on the usage of multiple large Legacy devices at the same time, causing delays in the progress of some research and renovation projects.

However, artisans have discovered another rare crystal in the Bahamar Highlands. This crimson crystal seems to be related somehow to the unique environment where it is found.
Legend has it that this is a Xeno Engram Catalyst formed under the influence of the witch Hruga's Xeno Engram.
Generally speaking, this medium affects humans and can cause psychological issues such as hallucinations, headaches, and anxiety.
But measurements show that given the extremely high Engram concentration of this crystal,
if the amount used is strictly controlled within safe limits, it can meet energy demands without causing obvious hallucinations in adults.
Under the current circumstances, this makes it a tempting alternative energy source.

The problem is that due to interference from the Creed, these types of crystals are still strictly prohibited from circulating on the market, as they are classified as Class II contraband.
Although the Guild has negotiated with the Creed and applied for a special-purpose usage permit for the translucent crimson crystals, it has still not yet been approved.

1031368.ReadingBookDes:
The revised edition contains thirty years' worth of adventure stories from the lives of famous treasure hunters. Not only does it still have the tales of the mysterious underwater hoard, the ruins lost to the river of time, and the Divine Legacy from the first edition, but it also adds three never-before-published secret records—including stories about the dazzling gems hidden in the mines above the highlands, the salvaging of the "Cursed Luno" from a deep-sea shipwreck, and details about how to crack Divine mechanisms. Every page hides truths that have been bought with lives.
Whether you are an adventure enthusiast, a treasure-hunting fanatic, or an ordinary reader curious about the "unknown," this revised journal will take you across mountains and seas and into secret realms to touch secrets buried by time, and to witness the experiences of treasure hunters living on the edge of darkness and light...

1031369.ReadingBookDes:
Date: ■■/■■/■■■■
Jayden, a treasure hunter from Byrnhalds, went missing at the seaside cliffs of the Asterleeds Plains. To this day, no trace of him has been found...

Date: ■■/■■/■■■■
Sarah, a treasure hunter from Asterleeds, was separated from her treasure-hunting squad in an underwater cave and has not been heard from since...

Date: ■■/■■/■■■■
Arat, a treasure hunter from Byrnhalds, was attacked by a beast while excavating a mountain cave. Only his belongings and a pool of blood were found at the scene. His whereabouts remain unknown...

...
...
...

If any kind soul has information regarding the above missing persons, please contact the address below. We will provide a generous reward...

1031370.ReadingBookDes:
Due to its geographical location, the highlands are sparsely populated and home to many highly aggressive beasts. Even among the domesticable Caprahorns, there are impulsive, wild varieties that will attack unprovoked.
The intention of this book is to help newcomers understand the potential dangers of the highlands and avoid any unnecessary incidents.
Be sure to stay away from areas inhabited by beasts. Even agile hunters only stay in designated hunting grounds, hunting docile foxes.
So, whether you are a passing merchant or a local resident, do not leave things to chance...

1031371.ReadingBookDes:
Chapter One: A Tale of Two Trends—From Noble Elegance to Street Rebellion
The story of Asterleeds' fashion begins with the collision of two vastly different yet mutually complementary cultures.

Chapter Two: The Nourishment of Regional Culture—Fashion Expression from Evening Wear to Daily Wear
The culture of the region has had a profound impact on Asterleeds' fashion. The diversity and pragmatism here always balanced "fashionability" and "adaptability." Whether it's a beach outfit for a summer stroll, a simple top for work, or an elegant dress for a wedding or special occasion, every ensemble manages to be both trendy and present styles well-suited to women's needs.

Chapter Three: Color Philosophy—From Classic Pairings to Trendy Color Blocks
The color selection for classic apparel always aligns with our core temperament, while closely following the most current trends. Foundational colors dominate, paired with soft floral tones, light pinks, mint greens, and other colors, exuding an elegant and gentle vibe.
Meanwhile, the color system for street brands is more "impactful." Highly saturated, striking colors serve as the main tone, paired with black, white, and other foundational colors to form strong visual contrasts...

1031372.ReadingBookDes:
Scarna, a down-and-out treasure hunter, unexpectedly obtains half of an ancient scroll marked "Divine Ruins." To unravel the secret of his ancestors, lost during their own hunt for treasure, he gathers companions with extraordinary skills—a genius artisan well-versed in mechanisms, an old scholar familiar with ancient texts and ciphers, and a highly skilled retired soldier.
The four-person squad sets off from a dangerous cliffside area. Along the way, they pass through poisonous miasma mazes in secret rainforests and the claustrophobic cabins of deep-sea shipwrecks, journeying through seemingly hopeless dangers to reach their destination—the place where the treasure is hidden. They must not only decipher the exquisite mechanisms left by their predecessors and fend off attacks from beasts and nature, but also face off in life-and-death struggles with other treasure hunters coveting the hoard.
During the journey, every treasure they discover hides forgotten secrets of history, and every crisis is accompanied by both trials and growth. As the truth gradually surfaces, they discover that what lies behind the treasure is not just wealth, but the forgotten legacy of a civilization, and a mission to protect it...

1031373.ReadingBookDes:
Hey! Over here! You're not gonna miss out on such an absurd yet spectacular performance, are you?
Just as the son of a wealthy man inherits his family's fortune, "siblings," abandoned in the past for a variety of reasons, pop up and demand a share of the estate.
The son knew he had one long-lost brother, but now two people stand before him claiming to be related to him.

"I'm your real brother! Look, I have the exact same birthmark as you!"
"Nonsense! I am your real brother! Look, I have a keepsake our father left for me!"

Which is the real one, and which is a phony? Who is telling the truth?
The massive fortune has drawn the eyes of schemers. To prevent the family estate from falling into the wrong hands, he must discern who his true brother is!
The secrets of a wealthy family, coming soon to the stage!

1031374.ReadingBookDes:
Father, you have always wanted me to inherit the family trade and become a tailor.
But I don't want to do that. I want to do something outside of the life plan you laid out for me.
You've always felt that being a treasure hunter is a shameful profession, because they're such a mixed bag of people: destitute refugees who can barely survive, desperate gamblers putting it all on the line—even profit-driven bandits. But Father, among them are also down-and-out scholars devoted to their research, travelers passionate about adventure, and historians who struck out on their own because their funding was denied.
I've learned so much from them. I'm endlessly fascinated by the knowledge I've gained, and I've fallen in love with the sights I see along my journeys.
But I also miss you. I miss seeing your face, and hearing your voice.
Perhaps you think I'm just acting on impulse, completely disregarding the legacy of our family trade—and maybe you as well, as you get older. But I want to say that isn't the case. I just want to choose something I truly love while I'm still young, instead of following the bog-standard, predictable path...

1031375.ReadingBookDes:
On the highlands, foxes shuttle through the woods and bushes, an ever-alert prey that hunters both revere and pursue. In the resource-scarce highlands, a fox is a treasure from head to tail—its thick pelt is an excellent material for fending off the bitter cold, as you can use it to make coats and line mattresses, while its meat serves as a rare source of nutrition. For hunters, foxes are an essential means of survival.
Using knowledge passed down through generations, hunters determine the size and age of their prey by the varying depths of their paw prints on the ground. From clues such as the gnawed remains of small animals and shed fox fur, they can deduce the fox's territory. They can even determine its current state based on its calls, such as its warning cries in the early morning or mating calls during breeding season.
Hunters are well aware of the fox's habits: they rest during the day and come out at night, foraging most frequently at dawn and dusk. They are adept at using the terrain for cover, and when faced with danger, they employ diversionary tactics, darting into the woods for a quick escape.
As you can see, becoming a skilled hunter is no easy task.

1031376.ReadingBookDes: Top secret clues, absolutely worth the price! Want to be one step ahead in unearthing treasures? Come to the Sunset Wilds—Silvan will tell you...

1031377.ReadingBookDes: There are scammers every year, but there are more than ever this year. I'll laugh for a lifetime at anyone who actually believes those ridiculous treasure clues!

1031378.ReadingBookDes:
Recently, a strange howling sound has been coming from the woods, but only in the middle of the night...

If you're not close to a campfire when it does, the sound will linger in your ears. You can't hear what it's saying, but you can feel the desolation within it...
It sounds like the cry of some beast, yet also like a person screaming.
Cover your ears, and find a well-lit place. That's the only way to drive off the sound nipping at your heels...

1031379.ReadingBookDes:
Beware of the pool. There was a rumor that many clues to a treasure can be found within—it drew countless treasure hunters here, determined to seize the key to the hoard.
One by one, they jumped into the water, never to come out again.
That's why you can often hear voices from within the pool, urging you to jump in.

Run! Don't believe them!
It's a trap!

1031380.ReadingBookDes:
Rumor has it that deep within the woods lies a terrifyingly massive monster. It's lived there for a long time, but none who've seen it have returned to tell the tale...
Scattered messages from its victims have been found along the country roads, all pointing to an exceptionally terrifying truth...

Never venture deep into the Sunset Wilds alone. Strange happenings always come in twos, after all.
Some say the masters of the treasure within the wilds are punishing the thieves coveting their wealth, while others say that the people who enter the woods disturb its peace.
Anyway—watch yourself!

1031381.ReadingBookDes:
Dear Thaddeus, are you doing well in Byrnhald? Have you heard the recent rumors? Yes, the ones about that treasure... I'm guessing you already know. ...Theoretically speaking, the tube-shaped detector the Cabbage Mission uses is not only viable—it might even be a work of genius.
Because the principle this detector utilizes isn't actually new. In the past, artisans referred to this method as "disturbance detection."
Simply put, it uses the source tropism that Xeno Engrams have toward regular Engrams (similar to how plants grow toward the sun) to locate Legacies. Even today, this method is still used by veteran artisans...

At the same time, this detector is actually quite forward-looking, in its own way. Normally, the Xeno Engrams in a crystal medium tend to be stable and present in small amounts, making them unlikely to generate any traction. But recently, the activity of various hallucinogenic media has seen an unexplained exponential increase. In this environment, if a small-volume medium is suspended in a cavity that isolates it from external disturbances, a clear traction phenomenon occurs. The crystal is attracted by the regular Engrams in the Legacy, causing it to strike the tube's walls, thereby allowing the Legacy to be detected.

Honestly, whoever came up with this idea must have a brilliant mind. After all, turning this principle into a truly usable device is the result of multiple intersecting disciplines.
First is energy dynamics, understanding the relationship between various Engram energies and Xeno energies. Next, one must understand the structural principles of Legacies, which is also the hardest problem to solve in this detector.
The principles mentioned before were just theoretical—there are often many other energies at work in an actual, external environment. The reason the Xeno Engram Catalyst gets pulled is that the detector utilizes certain internal Legacy components to create a relatively stable detection environment.
Finally, this person must also know a bit about gemology to choose a crystal rich in Xeno Engrams to serve as the medium.
Accomplishing all this is by no means easy. I don't even think many senior Legacy artisans would be able to pull it off. The simpler the principle of a device, the harder it often is to realize.

So in conclusion, rather than saying this detector was cobbled together by the Cabbage Mission, it's more likely... that some master is guiding them from behind the scenes. I would guess they deliberately made the device look rudimentary to cover their tracks.
Given the recent Vision-Sharing Society incident, I suggest we conduct further investigation into the Cabbage Mission.

1031420.ReadingBookDes:
Travelers of the Gloomy Depths, please be advised.
There have been many accidents here recently, with no small number of travelers finding themselves in dangerous situations. Although we've been able to rescue most of them, some have lost belongings, some suffered severe injuries, and some have even lost their lives.
The Gloomy Depths are not like other ruin caves where you can freely enter and explore at will. There are unspoken rules here. Some veteran travelers call this phenomenon the work of "evil spirits," but I prefer to think of them simply as "rules."
The ones we're aware of are listed below.
For the safety of you and your property, please be sure to abide by them. Don't overthink them.

Rule One
If you hear someone calling your name from behind, do not turn around.

Recently, two bizarre travelers have appeared in the Gloomy Depths.
They will often stop passersby on the road, questioning their purpose for coming here, and sometimes even preach a little...
It could be some strange organization conducting a survey. Still, even though they don't seem malicious at first glance,
best to avoid any potential trouble and ignore them.

Danger Level: Three stars.



Rule Two
If you see fog, dust, water ripples, fallen leaves, or gravel spinning into a triangular vortex, please leave the area immediately.

This phenomenon does not only appear near plants or rocks; sometimes it even appears on animals...
Some experienced travelers believe this to be an omen that the evil spirits that inhabit this place are about to manifest.
Regardless of what you believe, be sure to leave quickly.
Furthermore, do not discuss it with anyone. Don't even mention it.

Danger Level: Four stars.

1031421.ReadingBookDes:
Rule Three
If you feel a strong sense of déjà vu in the Gloomy Depths, do not look around for its source.

Most travelers, after entering this place, will experience déjà vu to some extent.
Some feel like they have been here before, while others believe they have suddenly lost a piece of their memory.
Some even claim that this kind of déjà vu can only be felt in illusions...
This leads them to hunt for evidence, for some kind of verification—and it always leads to an accident.
So, I'm warning everyone: do not delve into the source of the déjà vu. Simply treat it with a sense of reverence.
As I said, the Gloomy Depths are different from other ruins.
Any sort of in-depth investigation can very well destabilize your mind and displace your memories. It's already happened to many travelers.

Danger Level: Five stars.



Rule Four
If you are approached by strange people in green clothes, ignore them.

They are just ordinary treasure hunters. They have neither the intention nor the ability to harm anyone.
They may speak rudely, but don't worry—they're just trying to scare you.
There's also a possibility that they will invite you to join them... just ignore them.

Danger Level: Two stars.

1031422.ReadingBookDes:
Rule Five
Do not make any measurements in the Gloomy Depths.

In the Gloomy Depths, using tools like rulers for measuring is considered dangerous behavior.
But that's not all that I mean by measuring. I'm even talking about counting leaves, counting flowers, or tallying the number of bird calls you hear.
Once you take a measurement, even if you and your companion experience the same event simultaneously, you may get completely different results.

If you and your companion already have inconsistent measurement results, it means you've been targeted.
Find some plant ash as quickly as possible. Ignite it, and carry it with you as you make a swift exit.
During your departure, do not look back, no matter what.

Danger Level: Five stars.



Rule Six
If you notice the weather hasn't changed during your visit, don't mention it to anyone.

Because even if you do, most people won't understand what you mean, let alone believe you.
And if they do believe you, they might take it seriously, and try to investigate it for themselves here in the Gloomy Depths.
This violates the third rule.
In the Gloomy Depths, seriously thinking about certain things is often more dangerous than bumping into evil spirits.

This is exactly what several travelers we lost before were doing—sitting around,
discussing why the weather hadn't changed.
Afterward, they and their luggage vanished without warning. Not even their footprints were left behind.
It was as if they had never been here.
If you have already noticed something like this, please stop thinking about it immediately.

Danger Level: Four stars.

1031424.BookName: Don't Go to the Gloomy Depths
1031424.ReadingBookDes:
The Merchant Guild operating in the Gloomy Depths has a long history. In fact, it has been active there since the ruins were first discovered. On the surface, this Merchant Guild provides daily necessities to travelers. But if you actually go and count, there are probably more merchants operating there than real travelers shopping.

In truth, people haven't wanted to deal with them for a while now. The locals don't even like to mention them. It's a dangerous place, for one thing, with strange monsters and ne'er-do-wells springing up frequently. For another, anyone with a discerning eye can tell what they sell isn't just daily sundries. That's why people call them what they are now—the black market.
This raises the question: Given that the priests beneath the Pillar of Divinity abhor evil, how is it possible for the Guild to conduct dubious transactions right under their noses?

That brings us to the three leaders of the Merchant Guild. Rumor has it that these three jointly run this loose guild, but each of them has their own extraordinary background. One of them has ties to the Meowlux Merchant Guild and even once held a seat of power before an incident drove them to quietly retire. Another came from the Asterleeds Merchant Guild, highly experienced and with extensive channels. The last one is a mystery; it's said they're a local kingpin around the highlands who knows the Gloomy Depths inside and out.
Perhaps it's exactly because of these three leaders that this Merchant Guild has been able to skirt the edges of the rules and continue operating secretly until now.

On one hand, they only do business with regular customers. What you can buy and which tier of goods you can access all depend on your reputation within the Guild. Even if the Creed really wanted to take action, it would be hard to find a leverage point. On the other, they also strictly adhere to their bottom line—they never touch things obviously meant to harm or injure people.

The highlands area has always lacked supplies, and being situated in the border region between Byrnhald and Asterleeds, it's a sensitive zone that both sides keep quiet about. The emergence of such an unrestricted yet highly self-disciplined Merchant Guild has ironically gradually become part of the local ecosystem.

That's why veteran travelers often say:
Don't go to the Gloomy Depths if you don't have to; and if you really must go, at least know who you need to look for.

1031425.ReadingBookDes:
My Lady,
How have you been lately?

During these days away from the guild, I occasionally recall the times when we worked there together.
It's been a long time since I saw Maire. I wonder if she is still like before, always able to get passes for the mines.
She always did have better connections than I did.

Perhaps all the time I've spent out here has made it easier for me to remember some things.
Back at the academy, the teacher used to say I was too shortsighted, and that I would inevitably suffer great losses in business.
Thinking back on it now, those words weren't entirely wrong.
It's just that I always felt that properly managing the business at hand first wasn't a bad strategy either.

Business here in the Gloomy Depths is decent.
Although it doesn't earn much, I don't particularly dislike this feeling of wandering on the edges of the rules.
As you know, I've always hated being controlled, especially by those hypocritical rules of the council.
The Speaker always seemed to try and suppress merchants. Hard not to feel disgusted by it.

It's different here. This place is naturally suited for me. Everything depends purely on ability—survival of the fittest.
Ultimately, one must rely on business strategies and the goods themselves to do the talking.
Although you have to use a few little tricks from time to time, they're small in comparison to the lofty, obvious schemes of those council members.
I heard you'll be announcing a major move soon. You must let me know when so I can come and see it.

And don't forget to invite Maire. It's not often we get to share the same table, and it wouldn't be the worst thing to have a drink together.

Sabine
From the Gloomy Depths

1031426.ReadingBookDes:
My Lady,
Hope you've been well lately...

My days recently haven't been as peaceful as before.
The evil winds of the highlands have finally blown into my little corner.

A thorny problem has arisen within the Merchant Guild.
Edred proposed a suspicious partnership,
with the partner being none other than the notorious fellows in green that live up on the highlands.

He gave me his word that the partnership would only involve helping them fence goods,
and those green-clad folks were willing to offer a very substantial commission.

You couldn't ask for a better deal—
but everyone in the highlands knows about their organization.
I couldn't agree to it. The risk of such a partnership would be far too high.
Yet Gaston, that disappointment of a man, acquiesced, for some reason.
And so, the absurd partnership was pushed forward.

Some of my other subordinates have also tried to persuade me,
saying that if the Merchant Guild wants to grow, we must take some risks.
After all, this isn't the first time we've done so.

But for some reason, I can't shake the feeling that something isn't right.
It's an uneasiness that's hard to put into words.
Regardless, all I can do for now is put it to the side and let things play out.

I hope this all is just me overthinking.

P.S.: I haven't gotten any replies to my previous letters.
I guess you're probably busy and haven't had the time yet.
I shouldn't bother you too much...


But here's hoping you can spare a bit of time for me. I'd love to hear back from you.


Sabine
From the Gloomy Depths

1031427.ReadingBookDes:
My Lady,
Please find the time to read this letter, as it concerns a matter of grave importance.

As expected, the partnership has gradually devolved into an utter disaster.
Our partners' actions were too conspicuous, bringing the Creed to our doorstep
and nearly destroying the trust I worked so hard to build between us.
But that's nothing compared to that person's true goal in seeking us out.
He used the partnership to consolidate his power, and then refused to disclose any details regarding our partnership's accounting.
Gaston and I have gradually become mere rubber-stamping puppets...

Despite all my connections, I can't find out anything about his background.
None of the spies I sent out has returned. It sends shivers down my spine.
I'm getting the sense that he has someone truly powerful behind him,
and that he's been using the Merchant Guild as nothing more than a cover for his true intentions.

If this continues, I fear the Guild will suffer two heavy blows:
On one end, from the Creed coming to hold us accountable for our crimes. They could end our operations in the blink of an eye.
And on the other, from those powerful people behind our partners. They surely won't let us off easily.
I don't even dare think of what they might do.

So, as your old schoolmate...
My Lady, I beg you to use the power of the grand Guild to help me investigate this traitor's background.
At least let me know the specific contents of their transactions, the locations... any clues at all.
I cannot sit idly by and watch the Merchant Guild I built with my own hands be destroyed.

It's a matter of both responsibility and ideals.
You will surely understand me.

P.S.: My previous two letters have still received no reply.
Sometimes I even wonder
if these letters are even getting to you...

Regardless, I will still await your reply.
Once all these crises are resolved, I promise to come visit you in person to express my gratitude.

Sabine
From the Gloomy Depths

1031428.ReadingBookDes:
...Konrad has been acting particularly strange recently—talking erratically, like a person who's been totally exhausted for days.
The troublesome part is, this blabbering has turned into constant complaining from sunup to sundown.
Things like, "Gaston is a coward, he couldn't handle a little intimidation from Edred..." or "He's going to sell us all out..."

The more I think about it, the more I think Konrad might be plotting something crooked.
I mean, he's the one among us who is best at keeping secrets. All that prime stock we got before—it was all goods that he skimmed off the top of the ledgers.
Sure, on paper we're supposed to split the work between us. He acquires and stores the goods, and I sell them. But all the best stock is always with him!
What's more, he insists on stringing the goods together and carrying them around with him. You know, maybe he's just been pretending to be insane this whole time, and using it as an excuse to keep all the good stuff for himself!

Although, to be honest, he looks so delirious, I can't tell if he's just pretending or he actually has lost it.
Anyway, if I'm not around, just make sure he tones things down a bit around Gaston. And more importantly... keep an eye on the books. See if anything is missing. We'll be able to get a better read on Konrad after this all blows over.

1031429.ReadingBookDes:
Something serious has happened, just as I expected...
Konrad's ravings have gotten worse these past few days. He even started talking about our prime stock.
He's said things like, "Those prime goods aren't going to sell! They're just going to rot in our warehouse eventually." Not just that either, also "Doomsday is approaching, prepare for the aftermath!" and "There is a world inside the prime stock..."
I've kept him from over-indulging in Lallipar, but even that wasn't enough to shut his trap!

It would be fine if he just made a fuss in private, but one time, he actually said right to Gaston's face, "You can't sell that batch of prime stock. Just let me fence it for you!"
Gaston's face went pale...

Gaston's been giving us weird looks the past few days. I think he might already suspect we're up to something.
I think the best move is to make a quick escape before everything comes to light.
Things are different now, anyway. I don't think it'll be easy to move that product. Maybe we should just return it all to Gaston.
Even though Gaston can't do anything about Edred, if he decides to take us to task, we're in for it...

1031430.ReadingBookDes:
Listen, brother, now is not the time to be soft-hearted.
We have to hurry up and leave, just the two of us. We can't take Konrad.
He's already useless. I reckon his brain was ruined by the special goods. What a pity.

Don't think I'm saying all this out of nowhere, and don't think I'm crazy either.
Today I specifically went to find Marcel, and I asked him why he stopped buying the special goods. He said something changed with this stuff recently...
I can't exactly describe how it changed; his wording was too bizarre.
Anyway, the gist is that no matter how small you slice these special goods now, they cause hallucinations. Something or other inside them has grown exponentially for no reason.
In short, if you're exposed to them for too long, you become abnormal.

I figured what he said makes sense.
Do you remember? Konrad always hid the special goods close to his body, and he used to be perfectly normal.
His brain worked faster than all of ours put together.
One day, he suddenly said to me, "Hagen, can you hear these special goods talking..."
That was his first time acting crazy, and I was dumbfounded, you know?

...Later, he even said those red fragments had eyes and would stare at us or something. It was creepy.

Since then, he started being abnormal, saying all kinds of crazy things.
Insulting Gaston to his face, calling him a coward and stuff...
But even so, he still clung to those special goods and refused to throw them away. He's totally beyond saving.

Enough talking. Although we brothers have had times where we made big money, things are different now.
Yesterday I saw Gaston checking the ledgers... If we don't run now, we probably won't get another chance.
But if we bring a lunatic like him along, none of us will be able to escape.

1031431.ReadingBookDes:
The Creed Strikes Hard!!
—Destroying the Green Menace's Base and Recovering a Large Amount of Bapharian Legacies

Recently, the Cabbage Mission, a gang of outrageous ruffians that has long roamed the highlands, has finally faced justice.
A joint task force consisting of adventurers from the Pioneer Bureau and the Priest Guards successfully located and destroyed their hidden stronghold after days of hard work.

According to participants in the operation, the process of finding the hidden base was quite dramatic. While being chased by adventurers, a member of the Cabbage Mission fled in panic and actually chose to approach an Illusory Bloom to evade capture. The adventurers were forced to enter the illusion. Not only did they pull back the consciousness of this member—who preferred his brain burning out over facing justice—but they also deduced the base's specific location from the mixture of memory and reality within the illusion.
Subsequently, the Creed and the Pioneer Bureau launched a joint strike, successfully recovering a large number of illegal legacies, arresting several core members, and severely crippling the Cabbage Mission.

Follow-up verifications revealed that this panic-stricken Mission member is named Esher.
There were previous rumors claiming that he was an insider of the Creed. The Creed has officially clarified this: such claims are pure rumors; Esher is, in fact, a core member of the Cabbage Mission.

Further investigation indicates that most of those arrested are core members, and the severity of their crime is far more serious than that of ordinary idle members loitering in the highlands.
Judging by the confiscated blueprints and the quantity of legacies, the organization's operations were already quite mature, with strict internal rules and a tight structure.
It's worth noting that a batch of well-designed legacy modification blueprints was also found at the site. The precision of their drafting is so high that it rivals the design drawings of formal associations.

Insiders revealed that the organization referred to the legacies obtained through illegal excavation as "artifacts" and used them to advance some ulterior motive. Fortunately, the stronghold was destroyed in time. Otherwise, the consequences would be immeasurable. Based on this incident, it's speculated that there might be an actual mastermind behind the Cabbage Mission who has yet to surface.

Cedric, a priest of the Pillar of Divinity, hereby solemnly advises: If you accidentally discover a Bapharian Legacy during your explorations, please cease contact immediately and report it to the Creed at once. It will be uniformly disposed of by professionals.
Do not arbitrarily judge its nature, and definitely do not privately excavate Bapharian Ruins.

1031432.BookName: Research Notes on Symbiotic Plants I
1031432.ReadingBookDes:
I was woken up bright and early by Valerian, who asked me to go with him on a field study to the highlands.
He said he'd heard that a priest from the Creed had discovered a strange symbiotic plant next to an Illusory Bloom Crystal.

I scoffed right then and there.

Even interns know that the Xeno Engrams carried by an Illusory Bloom Crystal would devour regular Engrams around them.
No living thing could possibly survive under those conditions; even the soil where the Illusory Bloom takes root would become barren and cracked.
However, Valerian promised to treat me to Rainbean Rice and Bitter Orange Juice in Lallipar after the study, saying it was all-you-can-eat.
...I was tempted again.

Well, for the sake of food I haven't tried before, there's no harm in going to take a look.

—
When I actually arrived at the scene, I realized he hadn't been exaggerating.
Beneath that massive, eerie Illusory Bloom, the soil was indeed cracked and withered as I expected,
oozing an aura of danger and death.

Yet, under these conditions, a few plants were standing tall and straight.
This plant looked similar to a rockthistle, but lacked the rockthistle's flamboyant flowers. Instead, it looked more like an introverted herb.
The entire plant emitted a faint golden glow, leaving me shocked speechless...

—
On the other hand, Vivianne was the experienced one, and she just went right for it.
She tried moving one of the plants away from the Illusory Bloom, and its golden glow vanished immediately.
It seems it wasn't just surviving, but had formed some kind of stable relationship with the Illusory Bloom.
Not only was it not devoured by the Xeno Engrams, it actually used them as nourishment.

A saying from my seniors flashed through my mind:
Do not vainly attempt to measure nature with your shallow knowledge, nor try to understand it with human pity.
In the eyes of humanity, the Illusory Plague brought endless calamity to the highlands. But to nature, that might just be another form of normalcy.

—
...Right, a leopard can't change its spots, and Valerian still ended up playing a trick on me.
The taste of that Bitter Orange Juice... it wasn't meant for ordinary people at all. It's a beverage used by nearby pilgrims to stay awake.

1031433.BookName: Research Notes on Symbiotic Plants II
1031433.ReadingBookDes:
For the past few days, I have been immersed in studying this miraculous plant.
All its properties astound me; every observation challenges the rationality of existing Alchemy formulas.
I am really looking forward to seeing how high Master Mason's beard will curl up when he sees our research report.

—
Initial assessments suggest that this symbiotic rockthistle grass has immense application potential.
Although it rots quickly once it is separated from the main plant, that doesn't prevent it from being refined into crystals.
Once the crystals stabilized, we were amazed to find that
these crystals could still maintain their resonance effect with the Illusory Bloom.
In other words, the moment one falls into a hallucination, this crystal will light up with a golden glow.
It is just like lighting a beacon for a lost consciousness.

—

An even more bizarre phenomenon followed.
Even when refined into a crystal, the symbiotic rockthistle grass still retains some miraculous effect that has yet to be revealed.
Even when it has been separated into multiple crystals, they still maintain a certain connection with each other.
This reminds me of a phantom limb theory—
even if a part of the body is missing, its sensation still exists for a short time.

It's the same for these crystals.
If the same crystal originates from the same plant, they still retain a kind of response to each other.
When one of the crystals senses an illusion and emits light and heat, the other crystal reacts as well.
It's as if... they still maintain the same field even after separation.

—
This is the first time I have so clearly touched the boundaries of Alchemy.
I can vaguely feel that some structure outside of formulas is being pried open by us...
I'm starting to despise myself for being so lazy in the past,
and I also despise the schism between the Artisan Guild and the Imagine Research Institute.

—
I can't imagine what kind of cutting-edge creations would be born
if this were handed over to that master artisan who is proficient in the double-underline trend annotation method.

If he hadn't gone to the desert a year ago,
perhaps the Artisan Guild's current situation would be rewritten.
Maybe alchemists and artisans might no longer be divided, and would instead be working hand in hand.
Maybe they could unravel the mystery hidden behind this plant.

—
Forget it, let's stop these wild fantasies here.
Currently, we are restricted by the plant's extremely low yield, and it probably won't be enough to have a substantial impact on the world in the short term.

...Also, Valerian brought Bitter Orange Juice again today.
No matter how glib he gets, I'm not drinking another drop.

1031434.ReadingBookDes:
When the Gloomy Depths ruins were first discovered, it caused a shock in academia. Not only because of its bizarre structure that fused natural elements with ruins, but also because of the large number of rampaging Bapharian Oculoids active there.
Although it's been a considerable time since humanity learned about Bapharian Golems, their appearance in wild environments on such a scale is still quite rare. These Oculoids possess considerable destructive power, as well as a certain self-repair ability, and can achieve low-altitude hovering. To scholars, this might represent a crucial clue for reconstructing the history of the Bapharian Divines. And to artisans, this is undoubtedly a highly valuable location for Legacy research.

According to an artisan researching there, these Oculoids seem to possess a certain self-proliferation ability. When their numbers drop to a certain threshold, they are replenished again.
